revision_reason: V50 sharpened the Qwen3.5 hybrid-architecture carrier question by separating transient residual control from native Gated-DeltaNet recurrent state/write commitment. Exact-current main then added a noncanonical Trigger-2 renderer-transportability delta. V51 adds a distinct nonduplicate causal-interface discriminator: a decodable or steerable state is not yet a reusable Global J-Space interface. Recent primary work on forked futures and multi-slot entity tracking shows that current-answer decodability can collapse states that differ in future computation, and that linearly available information can remain unused by a natural consumer. Therefore J-Space promotion must test future-sufficient causal reuse against Shared, Local, Mixture, Distributed and structured-slot alternatives under exact checkpoint/runtime/renderer identity rather than treating one successful vector probe as global-workspace evidence.

external_research_delta.source: Ma et al. (2026), Hidden APIs in Language Models: Discovering Reusable Causal Interfaces from Forked Futures, arXiv:2607.27617
external_research_delta.finding: The study defines hidden-state equivalence by response distributions to future operations sampled only after a prefix state has formed, then compares Shared, Local, Mixture and Distributed interfaces under matched capacity and prequential causal description length. In the reported detailed evaluations Shared has the shortest held-out code for Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3-8B while maintaining similar future-signature fidelity; transplantation and mediation favor the recovered interface, but cross-family transfer is weaker and the blind model-organism audit retains a nonzero false-Shared rate.
external_research_delta.implication: Global J-Space/GWT should be treated as one falsifiable architecture class, not a default interpretation. Discovery must precede the future-operation cue, compare explicit nonshared alternatives, and require held-out future sufficiency plus causal consumption before shared-interface credit.

external_research_delta.source: Bogdan and Lindsey (2026), Slot Machines: How LLMs Keep Track of Multiple Entities, arXiv:2604.21139
external_research_delta.finding: The reported current-entity and prior-entity information occupies separate largely orthogonal slots. Prior-entity information can be linearly decodable while not being used for explicit factual retrieval, although it contributes to other relational behaviors.
external_research_delta.implication: Probe decodability is insufficient for natural-consumer credit. A useful J-Space may be structured or multi-slot, and each claimed slot/direction must be tested for the downstream operations that actually consume it.

external_research_delta.source: Xu (2026), Pattern Selectivity is Not Task-Causal Structure: A Cross-Architecture Mechanistic Study of Composed-Task Circuits in 1B-Class Language Models, arXiv:2606.05378
external_research_delta.finding: The reported matched screen-and-ablate study finds that the same composed task can rely on different primary causal attention-pattern screens across model families; behavioral similarity and pattern selectivity do not identify a portable task-causal circuit.
external_research_delta.implication: Any Trigger-2 J-Space circuit/vector claim remains checkpoint/runtime specific until cross-candidate causal transfer is directly measured. Pattern correlation or shared behavior cannot mint mechanism identity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A reusable Global J-Space state is better characterized by invariance of its downstream future-operation distribution than by current-answer decodability, current-token similarity, or one-step steering success.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: For the narrow Xeno/HCU operation set, current-state linear decodability plus a matched causal steering test may already predict all relevant future behavior, so a forked-futures assay adds complexity without materially changing state equivalence.
hypotheses.discriminator: Cache the exact model state before any consumer-operation cue, fork each prefix into a preregistered operation bank, compare future-response signatures, then test whether a low-dimensional candidate interface preserves held-out operation behavior better per matched complexity than Local/Mixture/Distributed alternatives.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Entity/binding information needed by Xeno may decompose into partially orthogonal role- or temporal-slots whose natural consumers differ; forcing one monolithic global vector can erase useful distinctions or create steering interference.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A single aligned low-dimensional shared interface is sufficient after the correct carrier and renderer are fixed; apparent slots are basis-dependent decompositions of one reusable shared subspace.
hypotheses.discriminator: Under the same rank/norm/parameter budget compare MONOLITHIC_SHARED versus STRUCTURED_SLOTTED_SHARED versus Local/Mixture/Distributed interfaces on future-signature fidelity, natural-use mediation, cross-operation interference and lesion/rescue selectivity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Even if a shared causal interface exists within one frozen Qwen3.5 candidate, its geometry and natural consumer paths will not transfer losslessly across BASE, POSTTRAINED and TARGET_MEASURED or across renderer variants.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The close ancestry of the three candidates preserves a stable shared causal quotient up to a simple alignment transform, allowing a common J-Space ABI after identity normalization.
hypotheses.discriminator: After per-candidate identity, renderer and carrier gates pass, preregister same-family and cross-candidate donor transplants with matched random/orthogonal controls and report both target correctness and donor-copy/locality failures.

fail_closed_rules: Current-answer or linear-probe decodability alone grants zero shared-interface credit.
One successful steering vector grants zero natural-use or global-workspace credit without consumer mediation/necessity evidence.
If Local, Mixture, Distributed or Structured-Slotted alternatives match Shared at the declared fidelity with equal or lower complexity, preserve NO_GLOBAL_SHARED_WINNER.
Cross-candidate transplant failure bounds the scope to the originating checkpoint/runtime/renderer identity; do not average failures away.
If a future-operation cue can be inferred from the cached prefix or metadata, invalidate that evaluation family.
